title: Module 1: The Counterfactual Problem
intro: What we mean when we say a programme caused an outcome, why the comparison we want can never be observed, and how the potential-outcomes model makes the problem precise.

title: Module 2: Selection Bias and the Identifying Assumption
intro: When the selection-bias term is zero, the difference between selection on observables and unobservables, and why controlling for things is not the same as identification.

title: Module 3: Causal Graphs: Confounders, Colliders, and Bad Controls
intro: Directed acyclic graphs as the tool that decides which variables to adjust for, the backdoor criterion, and the controls that make bias worse.

title: Module 4: Randomisation and the RCT
intro: Why random assignment zeroes selection bias, the ITT and LATE estimands, and the four threats (non-compliance, attrition, spillovers, external validity) that break trials in the field.

title: Module 5: Matching and Propensity Scores
intro: Building a comparison group under selection on observables, propensity-score and coarsened exact matching, common support, and why balance is the real test.

title: Module 6: Instrumental Variables
intro: Using clean variation in treatment, relevance and the untestable exclusion restriction, LATE and compliers, and why weak instruments mislead.

title: Module 7: Regression Discontinuity
intro: Identification at an eligibility cutoff, sharp and fuzzy designs, the local nature of the estimate, and the manipulation test that decides credibility.

title: Module 8: Difference-in-Differences
intro: The canonical 2x2, parallel trends and pre-trend plots, and the staggered-adoption problem with the Goodman-Bacon decomposition and modern estimators.

title: Module 9: Synthetic Control
intro: Constructing a counterfactual from a weighted donor pool for single-unit interventions, the centrality of pre-period fit, and placebo-based inference.

title: Module 10: Causal Machine Learning
intro: Estimating heterogeneous effects without fishing, causal forests and double machine learning, and the firm line that ML supplies flexibility, not identification.

title: Module 11: Reading and Interrogating an Evaluation
intro: A deliberate reading order and standing checklist, specification stability and publication bias, and the credibility debate (Banerjee-Duflo against Deaton and Pritchett) stated without false balance.

title: Module 12: When There Is No Counterfactual
intro: Credible evaluation without a comparison group: contribution analysis, process tracing, realist CMO, and QCA, and the standard of stating what would disconfirm the claim.

title: Module 13: Capstone Project
intro: Design and defend a credible evaluation for a real causal claim: estimand, design, identifying assumption, threats and checks, data and code, honest limits, and a one-page brief.
